content: Freedom is won by casting off greed, fear, and subservience to outside opinions.
author: Seneca
sourceWork: De Brevitate Vitae (On the Shortness of Life)
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. From childhood, we are trained to fit in, to smooth over our eccentricities, and to mirror the expectations of those around us. But copying others only buys superficial acceptance at the cost of your own soul.

Seneca understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Your unique perspective and lived contradictions are your greatest offering to the world. The moment you stop performing and stand firmly in your own skin, you command an authority that imitation can never manufacture.
reflectionPrompt: How does adopting this philosophical view alter the way you handle current friction?
